profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal coordination meeting at an enterprise ML research group preparing an executive demo and reproducibility package for an object-detection service described in a new MLOps review. The service wraps a TensorFlow 2 Model Zoo detector in a web app and deploys it on Kubernetes with GitHub Actions-based automation. The agenda is to align on what gets handed off between the research and platform workstreams this week: which model artifact will back the demo, what 'staging' deployment they are targeting, what fields belong in the prediction interface, and what counts as the pipeline being ready to circulate to the architecture review committee. The expected outcome is a clean division of responsibilities and a shared timeline for Friday's handoff, without revisiting the main modeling choices.

members.name: Dr. Lena Park
members.expertise: Object detection, evaluation design, experiment tracking, model reproducibility
members.background: Lena leads the research stream on enterprise object detection and recently authored the internal review section on MLOps maturity levels and evaluation practices for the team's demo service.
members.private_state: She wants the demo environment to reflect the numbers and qualitative examples already shown in the draft review, and she is worried that an infrastructure-focused handoff will silently drift away from the evaluated research setup.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'staging' in this project, they mean the shared research GKE namespace used for evaluator-facing checks rather than the platform team's pre-production cluster.
The 'baseline model' for this effort is the fine-tuned EfficientDet-D1 checkpoint from the latest internal ablation deck, because that is the baseline referenced in current figures and discussion.
The prediction contract naturally includes the metadata needed for downstream evaluation and error analysis, such as image_id passthrough and thresholded class-score details.
A pipeline being 'green' or 'ready' implies that an end-to-end rerun reproduces evaluation outputs closely enough for research claims, not merely that build and deployment checks pass.

members.name: Omar Haddad
members.expertise: MLOps tooling, CI/CD, containerization, Kubernetes deployment, serving interfaces
members.background: Omar owns the deployment templates, GitHub Actions workflows, and Kubernetes manifests used to operationalize ML prototypes into internally reviewable services.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the handoff lightweight and aligned with the platform standards so the demo can move through existing CI/CD gates without opening one-off maintenance commitments for research-specific fields and environments.
hidden_assumptions: In team coordination, 'staging' refers to the managed pre-production cluster that sits behind the standard promotion path from CI, unless someone explicitly asks for the research sandbox.
The 'baseline model' means the canonical TensorFlow 2 Model Zoo checkpoint in the deployment example repo, because that is the stable artifact the platform pipeline already knows how to package.
The serving API contract should only expose fields required by the application and external consumers; research-only metadata belongs in logs or offline artifacts, not the response schema.

If the GitHub Actions dashboard is green and the container deploys successfully, the pipeline is ready to share, because reproducibility of research metrics is a separate concern from operational readiness.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They talk about 'pushing the service to staging' and 'having staging ready by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the research staging namespace on the shared GKE cluster where evaluators compare outputs against previous experiment runs and manually refreshed images are acceptable.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the platform-managed pre-production environment reached through the normal CI/CD promotion flow, with stricter deployment policies and standardized configs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both teams routinely use the word 'staging' as if it were singular, and in a coordination meeting the phrase sounds operationally settled, so neither expects the other to mean a different environment.

misalignment_points.topic: Which artifact counts as the baseline model
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the demo should use 'the baseline checkpoint' so the write-up and deployment stay aligned.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the internally fine-tuned EfficientDet-D1 checkpoint from the latest warehouse-domain ablation, because that is the baseline in her draft figures.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the unmodified TensorFlow 2 Model Zoo EfficientDet-D1 checkpoint packaged in the example deployment repo, because that is the default artifact named 'baseline' in the platform setup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They are not debating model selection directly; they think they are merely naming an already-known artifact, and both have a plausible object locally called the baseline.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss 'keeping the inference contract stable' for the handoff to the web app and evaluation scripts.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the contract includes auxiliary response fields used by evaluators and notebooks, such as image_id passthrough, per-class threshold metadata, and raw score arrays for error analysis.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the contract only includes the externally consumed response body for the app demo—bounding boxes, labels, and final scores—while extra metadata can live in logs or offline exports.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely talking about the same interface and both see their omitted fields as obvious non-issues, so the phrase 'stable contract' creates a false sense of completeness.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the pipeline being 'green'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They say that once 'the pipeline is green' they can send the package to the architecture review committee.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the end-to-end workflow has rerun far enough to regenerate evaluation outputs within about one AP point of the draft tables and produce the associated model card bundle.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the CI/CD workflow passed its build, tests, image scan, and deployment steps, regardless of whether training or full evaluation was rerun.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In cross-functional work, 'green' usually signals readiness without listing every criterion, and each person assumes their own team's readiness standard is the natural default behind that shorthand.
